summary:
Space Trail is an educational browser-based cosmic runner game inspired by Subway Surfers. 

Following a distant stellar nova explosion, Astronaut Nova's spacecraft malfunctions mid-flight, stranding her across four celestial worlds: the Moon, Mars, Europa, and Titan. Players must jump and double-jump over space debris and alien patrols, collect four scattered mission pieces per stage, and gather meteor shower energy capsules (inspired by the Geminids, Perseids, and Leonids) to activate light-speed dash mode.

Each world simulates distinct gravitational physics and unlocks verified NASA and ESA astronomy fact cards upon completion, blending accessible arcade gameplay with real planetary science.
details:
Space Trail is a browser-based runner game about investigating a nova explosion. A distant star has exploded and its light is racing toward our solar system. The player runs across four worlds (Moon, Mars, Europa and Titan), jumps over rocks, collects four letter pieces in each world, and gathers energy orbs to fill a light-speed bar. When the bar is full, the player can pass through obstacles at light speed.

Benefit and intended impact: the game teaches real facts about each world while players have fun. For example, the Moon’s gravity is about one sixth of Earth’s, a Mars day lasts about 24 hours 37 minutes, Europa may have an ocean under its ice, and Titan has lakes of liquid methane. Each world also has its own gravity and speed, so players can feel the differences.

Tools: HTML, CSS and JavaScript (canvas) in a single file. It needs no installation and runs on phones and computers in a browser.

Creativity: it combines a story about a stellar explosion with a simple runner game and real space facts.
